---
title: The big picture
subtitle: What BDM is, in one sitting
aliases: [/explanations/index.html, /why/ecosystem.html]
---

BDM (Behaverse Data Model) is a way to organize everything a behavioral
experiment produces — responses, questionnaires, event streams, physiological
signals — into one predictable, self-describing dataset. A BDM dataset is an
ordinary folder: tidy tables and event streams whose names, columns, and
units follow shared conventions, together with the metadata that explains
what they are and how they came to be.

Three ideas carry the whole model: data comes in **three levels**, a dataset
is a **folder with a fixed anatomy**, and the data model is one piece of a
**small ecosystem**. Everything else on this site is detail behind one of
these three.

## Three levels of data

A BDM dataset separates what was observed, what it means, and what we
conclude from it — three levels, each derived from the one below:

[Events](/spec/event/index.qmd) (and [timeseries](/spec/timeseries.qmd))
: The raw record: what happened, as it happened. Key presses, stimulus
  presentations, answers given — timestamped event streams — plus continuous
  signals (EEG, eye tracking) stored alongside them. Detailed enough to
  reconstruct the experiment.

[Trials](/spec/trial/index.qmd)
: The scientific unit of analysis. A trial is not observed — it is derived
  from the events by an explicit, task-specific rule, and stored as tidy
  tables (responses, stimuli, options, …). The same event stream can yield
  different trial tables under different rules, which is why BDM keeps the
  events and records how the trials were derived.

[Models](/spec/models/index.qmd)
: What the data tells us: summary statistics, scores, and fitted models of
  the agents, derived from trials or directly from events.

Most formats keep only a trial-level table and discard the rest. Keeping the
three levels distinct and linked is what makes a BDM dataset auditable: a
conclusion traces back to the trials it was computed from, and a trial traces
back to the raw events it was derived from.

## The anatomy of a dataset

A BDM dataset is a folder with a predictable shape:

```
my-study/
├─ README.md            # the dataset card: what this is, who, how, license
├─ LICENSE
├─ instruments/         # what was used to collect the data
├─ agents.csv           # who the data is about
└─ data/                # one folder per agent / session / activity
   └─ agent_001/
      └─ session_1/
         └─ stroop/
            ├─ events_1.ndjson   # level 1: what happened, as it happened
            ├─ response_1.csv    # level 2: trials, one row each
            └─ stimulus_1.csv
```

Around the data files, three artifacts explain them: the **[dataset
card](/spec/dataset-cards.qmd)** (the `README.md` front matter: what this
dataset is, who made it, and a codebook for its variables), the
**[studyflow](/spec/studyflows.qmd)** (the study design: which activities, in
what order), and the
**[instruments](/spec/conventions/folder-structure.qmd)** (the tasks and
questionnaires used, with their parameters).

Every table is tidy; every name follows the [naming
conventions](/spec/conventions/naming.html); every column is defined in the
[specification](/spec/index.html). You always know where things are and what
they are called. (The full layout, including timeseries files, is in the
[folder structure](/spec/conventions/folder-structure.qmd) specification.)

## Where everything fits

BDM is one piece of a set of standards and tools that work together:

| Piece | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Data model** (this site) | The human-facing framework: conventions, concepts, guides, specification | [behaverse.org/data-model](https://behaverse.org/data-model) |
| **Schemas** | The machine-readable source of truth: JSON Schemas, field definitions, validators, changelogs | [behaverse.org/schemas](https://behaverse.org/schemas) · [GitHub](https://github.com/behaverse/schemas) |
| **Studyflow modeler** | Visual editor for study designs (studyflows) | [behaverse.org/studyflow-modeler](https://behaverse.org/studyflow-modeler/app) |
| **Behaverse** | The broader project: cognitive assessments, games, models | [behaverse.org](https://behaverse.org) |

How they relate: this site **defines** the prose conventions and renders
summaries; the schemas repository **owns** every machine artifact (this site
fetches them at build time, pinned by `schemas.lock`); tools consume both.
A public catalog of BDM-formatted datasets will follow the first published
reference dataset — see the [roadmap](/roadmap.qmd).

Within this site, the deep dives are one click away:

- The **rules** — naming, indexing, units, folder structure — live in the
  [Specification](/spec/index.html), alongside the field-by-field reference
  for every table.
- The **reasoning** behind the design lives here in Concepts:
  [design process](design-process.qmd) ·
  [the nature of behavioral data](behavioral-data.qmd) ·
  [metadata](metadata.qmd).
